South Elizabeth Seychelles Hospital INTERNAL MEDICINE DEPARTMENT Location: 4923 Olivia Parkway Suite 217, Lake Jennabury
PATIENT: Lysander Fairfax Phone: 28451903 email:bradleymorgan@example.org DATE OF BIRTH: 1947-05-12 AGE: 79 years
FOLLOW-UP DATE: 07/27/27 FOLLOWED BY: Dr. Emily Carter
CHIEF COMPLAINT
Follow-up visit for COPD management, evaluation of persistent edema, and ongoing mental health treatment.
HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Mr. Lysander Fairfax returns for a follow-up visit approximately six weeks after his last appointment. He reports that while he has continued the pulmonary rehabilitation program as recommended, he has experienced only marginal improvements in his overall respiratory function. He notes that his reliance on the albuterol inhaler remains at six to seven times per day, particularly during physical exertion. Mr. Fairfax mentions that he has been adhering to his corticosteroid regimen, but he remains concerned about the persistent nature of his symptoms.
In addition to respiratory concerns, Mr. Fairfax's bilateral lower extremity edema has shown minimal change despite adherence to the increased furosemide dosage of 120 mg daily. He describes the edema as still being at a 3+ pitting level and expresses frustration over its impact on his mobility and quality of life. He has been following dietary sodium restrictions as advised.
Regarding his mental health, Mr. Fairfax reports that he has been participating in cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) sessions, which he finds beneficial in managing his anxiety related to health concerns. He states that while his mood has improved, he still experiences fluctuations in anxiety levels, particularly in relation to his physical health status.
REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
General - + persistent fatigue, no fevers or chills. Pulmonary - + persistent dyspnea, + decreased nocturnal wheezing, - cough, - sputum production, no hemoptysis. Cardiac - no chest pain or palpitations, + orthopnea. Gastrointestinal - no nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea. Musculoskeletal - + ongoing joint pain, no swelling. Neurological - no dizziness or headaches.
PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
1. Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) 2. Hypertension 3. Osteoarthritis 4. Persistent fatigue 5. Anxiety and depression (ongoing management)
PAST SURGICAL HISTORY
1. Right knee arthroscopy in 2018.
FAMILY HISTORY
Father - history of lung cancer. Mother - history of hypertension.
SOCIAL HISTORY
Lives alone in , . Former carpenter, now retired. Quit smoking 15 years ago. Occasional alcohol use. No illicit drug use.
ALLERGIES
No known drug allergies.
MEDICATIONS ON FOLLOW-UP
1. Albuterol inhaler as needed, currently using six to seven times daily. 2. Lisinopril 20 mg daily. 3. Fluticasone/salmeterol 500/50 MDI, 1 puff twice daily. 4. Tiotropium 18 mcg inhaler, 1 puff daily. 5. Acetaminophen 500 mg as needed for pain. 6. Furosemide 120 mg daily (unchanged). 7. Sertraline 100 mg daily.
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital Signs: T 98.7F, HR 82, BP 130/76, RR 26, O2 sat 80% on room air
General: Elderly male in moderate respiratory distress, appears fatigued but more engaged than prior visits. HEENT: No nasal congestion, oropharynx clear. Pulmonary: Diminished breath sounds bilaterally, moderate wheezing noted on expiration, no crackles. Cardiac: Regular rate and rhythm, no murmurs. Extremities: 3+ pitting edema in bilateral lower extremities, no erythema or warmth.
LABORATORY DATA
1. CBC: WBC 9.1, Hgb 10.4, Hct 31.0, Plt 215 2. BMP: Na 130, K 4.1, Cl 99, CO2 30, BUN 32, Cr 1.9, Glucose 92 3. BNP: 650 (slightly increased). 4. Thyroid function tests: TSH 3.2 (within normal limits).
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. COPD management: Mr. Fairfax continues to experience significant respiratory symptoms despite participation in pulmonary rehabilitation. An increase in the fluticasone/salmeterol inhaler to 2 puffs twice daily is recommended to better control his symptoms. A follow-up pulmonary function test is advised to assess the current status of his lung function. 2. Hypertension: Continue lisinopril. Blood pressure remains stable. Follow-up in 1 month. 3. Lower extremity edema: The edema persists despite the current furosemide dosage. Referral to nephrology is recommended for further evaluation of renal function and potential adjustment of diuretic therapy. Reinforcement of dietary sodium restrictions continues to be essential. 4. Mental health: Mr. Fairfax reports benefits from CBT. Continue sertraline 100 mg daily. Follow-up with psychiatry in one month for ongoing management and reassessment of treatment efficacy.
Patient education reiterated regarding the importance of recognizing exacerbation signs, adherence to medication, and lifestyle modifications to effectively manage COPD and edema.
